name: OmniQuery Planner
target_user: Database Systems Engineers and Compiler Researchers
problem: Traditional database cost-based optimizers hide their search space exploration and rewrite heuristics, making it impossible to study alternative plan generation and rule-based transformations without reading a monolithic commercial codebase.
pain: Database engineers cannot easily inspect how relational algebra trees are transformed into execution graphs or how join-order dynamic programming behaves under different cardinality estimators.
solution: A zero-dependency relational query optimizer written in Java 21. It features a custom SQL-to-RelNode parser, Volcano/Cascades style equivalence-class rule engine, memoized search space container, and dynamic cost estimator.
verification: Deterministic integration suite feeding malformed relational expressions, cyclic join graphs, and zero-cardinality catalog statistics to verify robust optimizer fallback and cost bounds exceptions.
major_features: Custom relational algebra parser converting SQL projections, selections, and inner joins into explicit AST nodes
Memoization table architecture storing equivalent logical and physical expression trees with shared sub-plans
Rule-based transformation engine supporting predicate pushdown, constant folding, and join reordering
Cost-based exploration framework utilizing catalog statistics histograms to score physical execution plans
Dynamic programming join-order enumerator implementing Left-Deep and Bushy tree search spaces
Volcano-style property enforcer ensuring required sort orders and physical distribution traits are met
Plan visualizer generating hierarchical string representations and structural cost breakdowns for debugging
Deterministic verification harness validating optimizer output stability against mutated cardinality inputs
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
